content.text: If there were a transitive containment property, it could make walking the resources in a Fedora repository easier.
It might be useful to store pairs of resources being compared, before and after import or export, in a dictionary.
It might be worthwhile to consider implementing options for verification implemented for BagIt, e.g.:
https://github.com/LibraryOfCongress/bagit-java
Are you suggesting that Fedora should create its own transitive containment property independent of LDP?
It might be useful to store pairs of resources being compared, before and after import or export, in a dictionary.
By that you presumably mean the
identifiers
of such resources?
Transitive versions of containment properties could be useful for SPARQL queries with aggregate functions or with restrictions on descendants.
I reviewed some of the prior discussion with interest:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/hydra-tech/gEEfQ4-ctUE/mZx9rMgOAgAJ
The issue is also discussed in Semantic Web for the Working Ontologist (Chp. 8).
I think there are some contexts in which containment should not be problematic: file paths, spatial, temporal, ...
I don't know if there are other means to achieve the same result in Fedora or if there would be negative consequences.
Yes, the identifiers. Thanks for the clarification.
I updated the code base to integrate
's code. Also cleaned the code up a bit.
I created a PR for this and merged it already, so if someone wants to see exactly what I changed, you can:
https://github.com/bseeger/fcrepo-sample-dataset-tests/pull/3
It would be great if someone else can run this tool and test out the instructions in the README.
Hi

, a quick question: does your earlier comment about this not yet working against binaries still apply?  I running this against a set of sample rdf + binaries and getting some errors. In particular I get an error:
TypeError: iter() returned non-iterator of type 'FileSource'".

This may be something python3 specific as I am running under 3 (after converting with the 2to3 utility, and then changing ConfigParser to configparser – not sure why that name change is not caught by the converter).  Anyway, long story short, I wasn't able to install all the dependencies under 2 so was trying under 3, but in light of the issues maybe I will revert to 2.
Hi
I went so far as to install python3, but haven't run this code with it yet.  I'll try that now.
Testing binaries is now functional  - this is probably a python 2 to 3 issue.    (I hope.

OK. I will revert to testing in 2.  For some reason I cannot get rdflib to install correctly under a v2 virtualenv, so was trying to get around that, but that was probably a bad idea since it introduces other potential for problems.
- I have a commit I just pushed – so you can stay with three.  Just fetch master again.
That configparser thing is a pain though - that makes it very specific to either python 2 or 3.  What do people do about that?  Right now I left it as the python3 version.
- and thank you for testing it!  I'm not proud of that code, but it functions.
Success!  I have successfully verified an export under Python 3!  This is great – I particularly like the logging feature.
I'm getting all 100 binary checksums not matching, though.  Is this your experience too?  You mentioned earlier that you had discovered binary corruption issues upon export.
I'm also still hitting the "TypeError" mentioned above when I run "both".  I suspect that this could be some error in the data that is not being caught in time and leads to the type error.

Great!  Are you using the latest version of the import-export tool?  There was corruption upon export at one point, but it was fixed a while back, so binaries should work fine.  That being said, I've only worked with jpegs and png files - what mimetype are your binaries?

And now that I think of it, I didn't test any binaries today, so I could have had a regression in the code. I was using the LUBM dataset for testing today.  I'll look into this over the weekend (feel free too, if you have the time).
Cool. I'll keep testing and tinkering.
My binaries are PDFs.

EDIT: in the plant patents there are external resources (i.e. MIME type message external body), and those are the resources that are causing the error.  I will check with the developer team about what the expected behavior is there.
I thought I had the latest import/export tool, but will double-check.
Great test - I had not tested that scenario nor accounted for it at all in the code.   I think the binary file is a placeholder for these external resources (
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/pull/41)
- perhaps the test needs to work around it, but we can see what folks say on the tech list.
Were you able to run import on LUBM_02? Export worked fine.
This ticket has been overtaken by
in that the consolidated verification tool will already integrate a walker like the one described in this ticket.
Resolved by:
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2284
The goal of this ticket is to integrate this code:
https://github.com/jwestgard/fcrepo-sample-dataset-tests/blob/master/walk_fcrepo.py
into this code:
https://github.com/bseeger/fcrepo-sample-dataset-tests/blob/master/fcrepo-import-export-tests/verify/source.py
Specifically in the HttpSource class (which is an iterator already, or at least attempts to be ;).
There may be some need to tweak the main code once this integration happens.  Please feel free to contact
for help with this.
